items.canonical_answer: The value of final goods and services produced within a country’s territory during a specified period, avoiding double counting.

items.canonical_answer: Domestic product adjusted for net factor income from abroad by residents under the stated convention.
marking_guidance: Definition/key term (1): Domestic product adjusted for net factor income from abroad by residents under the stated convention.
objective_titles: Describe Gross National Product

items.canonical_answer: Income earned by a country’s factors of production over a stated period, with the accounting measure specified.
marking_guidance: Definition/key term (1): Income earned by a country’s factors of production over a stated period, with the accounting measure specified.
objective_titles: Describe National Income

items.canonical_answer: Measuring production by summing value added or final output on a consistent basis without double counting.
marking_guidance: Definition/key term (1): Measuring production by summing value added or final output on a consistent basis without double counting.
objective_titles: Describe output method of national-income measurement

items.canonical_answer: Measuring production by summing factor incomes earned from it on a consistent basis.
marking_guidance: Definition/key term (1): Measuring production by summing factor incomes earned from it on a consistent basis.
objective_titles: Describe income method of national-income measurement

items.canonical_answer: Measuring production by summing final spending on domestically produced output, with the appropriate external adjustment.
marking_guidance: Definition/key term (1): Measuring production by summing final spending on domestically produced output, with the appropriate external adjustment.
objective_titles: Describe expenditure method of national-income measurement

items.prompt: Identify the domestic measure and the national measure in these descriptions: final output inside the territory; domestic output adjusted for net resident factor income from abroad.
items.canonical_answer: GDP is the territorial measure; GNP is the adjusted national measure.
marking_guidance: Feature/characteristic (1): first requested boundary, category or amount. Distinction/example (1): second correct element with its economic meaning.
objective_titles: Define Gross Domestic Product, Gross National Product and National Income

items.prompt: Identify the location test and output boundary for GDP using an invented foreign-owned factory making final furniture inside Namibia.
items.canonical_answer: Production is inside the territory and final furniture counts without double counting; foreign ownership does not exclude it.
marking_guidance: Feature/characteristic (1): first requested boundary, category or amount. Distinction/example (1): second correct element with its economic meaning.
objective_titles: Describe Gross Domestic Product

items.prompt: Identify the two flows needed to adjust GDP into GNP under a stated factor-income convention.
items.canonical_answer: Relevant factor income received from abroad and corresponding factor income paid abroad; subtract payments from receipts.
marking_guidance: Feature/characteristic (1): first requested boundary, category or amount. Distinction/example (1): second correct element with its economic meaning.
objective_titles: Describe Gross National Product

items.prompt: Identify two earned factor-income categories, distinct from a support transfer.
items.canonical_answer: Wages and rent are earned factor incomes; a transfer without current production in exchange is not another factor reward.
marking_guidance: Feature/characteristic (1): first requested boundary, category or amount. Distinction/example (1): second correct element with its economic meaning.
objective_titles: Describe National Income

items.prompt: Identify two distinct national-income measurement approaches and the aspect each records.
items.canonical_answer: Output records value added; income records factor earnings.
marking_guidance: Feature/characteristic (1): first requested boundary, category or amount. Distinction/example (1): second correct element with its economic meaning.
objective_titles: Describe the different methods of calculating the national income

items.prompt: Identify the value added at each stage where an invented grower sells for N$100 and a processor buys that input then sells final output for N$250, with no other intermediate inputs.
items.canonical_answer: Grower value added N$100; processor value added N$150. Their sum equals final N$250.
marking_guidance: Feature/characteristic (1): first requested boundary, category or amount. Distinction/example (1): second correct element with its economic meaning.
objective_titles: Describe output method of national-income measurement

items.prompt: Identify two receipts excluded from newly earned factor income: a new loan, wages for current work, a support transfer.
items.canonical_answer: The loan is financing and the support transfer is not a current-production reward; wages are factor income.
marking_guidance: Feature/characteristic (1): first requested boundary, category or amount. Distinction/example (1): second correct element with its economic meaning.
objective_titles: Describe income method of national-income measurement

items.prompt: Identify the treatment of exports and imports in final expenditure on domestic output.
items.canonical_answer: Include exports of domestic output; exclude imports so foreign output is not counted as domestic production.
marking_guidance: Feature/characteristic (1): first requested boundary, category or amount. Distinction/example (1): second correct element with its economic meaning.
objective_titles: Describe expenditure method of national-income measurement

items.prompt: Explain how a consistent real national-output series can help assess economic performance when current-price totals may reflect inflation.
items.canonical_answer: Using a common price basis separates production changes from general price increases. The real series can show expansion or slowdown, informing policy investigation; it does not by itself prove a particular policy caused the change.
marking_guidance: Starting change (1): real series available. Because/mechanism (2): price effect separated (1), real activity trend identified (1). Consequence (1): informs assessment without sole-cause inference.
objective_titles: Explain reasons for measuring the national income

items.prompt: Explain why an increase in total real output does not alone show higher average living standards when population grows faster.
items.canonical_answer: Real output per person can fall despite a larger total. Distribution, environmental costs and other welfare conditions also affect living standards.
marking_guidance: Context (1): population grows faster. Reason/conclusion (1): per-capita output and other welfare conditions prevent total-only inference.
objective_titles: Explain reasons for measuring the national income

items.prompt: Define GDP (2). Identify two national-income measurement methods (2). Explain one use of a consistently measured real-output time series (2). Identify the measures in these descriptions: output within the territory; domestic output adjusted for net factor income from abroad (2).
items.canonical_answer: GDP values final goods and services produced within the territory over a period. Output and income are methods. A real series separates price effects to assess production changes and inform policy. The descriptions identify GDP and GNP respectively.

items.prompt: Invented simplified annual production chain with no other intermediate inputs: grower sells produce N$100 to a processor; processor sells final output N$250 to households. The grower generates wages N$70 and profit N$30; processor generates wages N$90 and profit N$60. All entries use the same period, domestic coverage and valuation, with no tax, capital-consumption allowance or abroad adjustments needed in this illustration. A separate real-output series is available for policy assessment. Describe three measurement features, each with a distinguishing detail from the case (6). Explain why summing value added rather than all sales gives useful consistent output evidence (4). Explain how the income and expenditure methods connect to that output including a use of the real series (4).
items.canonical_answer: The domestic account covers territorial production; output value added is N$100 plus N$150; income is wages N$160 plus profit N$90. Final household spending is N$250. Adding sales N$350 would repeat the input N$100, whereas value added gives N$250 once. The matched income and expenditure views also give N$250, enabling a consistency check. A real series can assess production change rather than price increases, without proving policy causation.
marking_guidance: Context/data description (6): domestic coverage (1), same territory/period detail (1); output method (1), N$100+N$150 detail (1); income method (1), wages N$160/profit N$90 detail (1). First explanation (4): all sales total N$350 (1), input N$100 repeated (1), value added N$250 avoids it (1), useful consistent production evidence (1). Second explanation (4): income N$250 (1), final spending N$250 (1), same activity rather than added totals (1), real series helps assess quantity trend not merely prices (1). Marks allocation 6+4+4=14.
